The typical monthly payment on a new U.S. home just fell to $2,723 — its lowest in nearly two months — and buyers suddenly hold the cards.

Redfin's latest weekly update (four weeks ending Nov. 15) puts the median U.S. home-sale price at $388,516, down 0.4% from a year ago — the fourth straight week of declines after three years of nonstop increases. The $2,723 payment, at a 7.11% average rate, is down from $2,760 a week earlier, though still 8.2% higher than last year.

The real shift: there are now over half a million more sellers than buyers nationwide — what Redfin calls the strongest buyer's market in its records back to 2013. One in five listings (20.7%) has already cut its price.

My take: when sellers outnumber buyers by half a million, the list price is a starting line, not the finish. If you're shopping, ask for the discount — this market is built to give it.

Would a lower monthly payment get you off the sidelines? 👇
